determinism_evidence.notes: Two consecutive builds of unchanged source completed successfully but produced different PDF hashes. This confirms the manuscript's non-byte-determinism claim. The build log contained Overfull hbox warnings and an h-float warning, but no LaTeX errors.

findings.finding: The manuscript compiles successfully through the repository build script and produces a PDF; no fatal LaTeX error occurred.
The build is successful but not warning-free: the log reports multiple Overfull hbox warnings for the long DOI table entries and one float-placement warning.
The build script writes the SHA-256 of the produced PDF to .build.sha256, and on the second observed build the recorded hash matched the PDF hash exactly.
The manuscript's claim that byte-for-byte reproducibility is not achieved is confirmed: consecutive unchanged-source builds yielded different hashes.

The Gamma-family provenance is traceable to the cited packages, but the source corpus itself is internally inconsistent: DOI 31942821 metadata describes the saturating rho/(rho+rho_crit) form while its key_result and source code implement the rho^(3/2)/(rho+rho_crit) Scenario B form; DOI 31942800 provides the square-root Scenario B+ form. The manuscript correctly presents this as a bifurcation and does not claim demonstrated supersession.

The KC1 status claim is traceable and supported as an open provenance issue, not an executed result: the cited package records null delta_chi2/significance and no new fit, while retaining the conditional >=5 sigma criterion.

The gravitational-wave/electromagnetic luminosity-distance discriminator is traceable to the relativistic-action package and its preregistration, but remains proposed and unexecuted; the source package reports no dataset and null fit/significance fields.
